summary: In the proof of Claim 7, the induction falsely assumes that for each $Y_i$, two non-adjacent vertices $z_i', z_i'' \in N^{\mathrm{Int}}(Y_i)$ lie in $J_m$, but $J_m$ is merely an arbitrary independent set of size $k$ in $G_{\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{Big}}}$ and cannot be guaranteed to contain two vertices from each $N^{\mathrm{Int}}(Y_i)$.

In the base case of the induction, moving the token from $y_1''$ to $z_1'$ is invalid because $z_1' \in C_{Y_1}$ is adjacent to $y_1'$, which still holds a token in $I_s$, violating the independent set condition.
The proof erroneously cites Claim 4 (which bounds the order of $G$) instead of Claim 5 to justify reconfiguring tokens on linear forests.
